answer: The predicted probability of achieving efficacy PR at age 65 with treatment is approximately 0.97 (≈97%; effectively near 1). Primary estimate from a Firth-penalized logistic regression of PR (PR=1 vs SD/PD=0) on Age, fit in the treatment group (Groups==1, n=41): P(PR | age 65) = 0.969. Important caveat: the treated group exhibits complete separation — all 41 treated patients achieved PR (0 SD/PD) — so the unpenalized MLE does not exist and the within-group data cannot support any age gradient; the near-unity prediction reflects the group's uniformly perfect response rather than an age effect (the Firth age coefficient is slightly negative, −0.038/year, and is not a reliable effect estimate under separation). Sensitivity (secondary context): a pooled plain logistic regression on all 80 patients (PR vs SD/PD, age only) gives P(PR | age 65) = 0.395.
